requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions.content` states only what the instructions text must say. It must tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting. It must explain how to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence. It must explain how to pass `used: []` when none contributed. It also states that finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.

I checked each clause for a structural obligation: a required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. None of them has one. Every clause constrains the observable content of the `instructions` string. A different implementation could build the string inline, take it from a constant, or generate it from a template. Each would produce the same text and still satisfy the requirement. So how the text is built is discretionary.

The parent requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` governs when the field is delivered. That is also observable behavior, and the subject only cites it for context. Because no structural obligation exists, no implementation root is needed. The empty review roots are therefore not a gap. Whether the text content is adequately tested belongs to the behavioral criterion, which this review does not cover.

behavioral: The subject requires the first-search `instructions` text to cover four things. These are: call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting; how to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence; how to pass `used: []` when none contributed; and that finishing records the selected inputs without fetching more source.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It reads `instructions` from the first `search_text` result, which is an empty-match result. It asserts that the text contains each of these phrases:
- "Before submitting, close every delivered search page" covers the obligation to finish every delivered page before submitting.
- "finish_search" names the tool to call.
- "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read" covers how to select tags.
- "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" covers passing `used: []` when none contributed.
- "without reading more source" covers that finishing fetches no more source.

The test also checks that a structural search from a fresh session carries identical instructions. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field. The test also exercises `finish_search` itself: it records the selected dependencies and returns no more source. Together these confirm the described behavior. No other observable obligation is in scope, and the delivery rules belong to the parent requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`. The assertions check the content the requirement names, so I found no gap.
